findings.source_quote: et dic omnibus in magno honore esse eum et dignitate apud Dominum, et magnae potestatis eum praesidem esse et potentem in officio suo.
findings.english_quote: Tell everyone that he has great honor and dignity before the Lord. He presides with great authority and is powerful in his role.
findings.issue: The Latin makes both the shepherd’s honor and his powerful presiding role contents of the instruction to tell everyone. The simplified wording explicitly places only his honor within that instruction, turning the authority-and-role clause into a separate assertion. The information survives, but the instruction’s full scope does not.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Tell everyone that he has great honor and dignity before the Lord. Also tell them that he presides with great authority and is powerful in his role.”

summary: The standard edition faithfully covers the selected Latin and can be accepted. The simplified edition independently preserves the substantive assertions, conditions, dialogue, and repentance terminology, but needs a small correction to the scope of the reporting instruction. Both editions appropriately disclose the contextual judgment behind “patience” and avoid claiming Amherst support for this section. This assessment concerns the supplied working text and attributed reports, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation; the proposed replacement remains subject to fresh review.
